title: Amin Naseri Arrested by Security Forces
content:
According to HRANA, Amin Naseri was arrested in the city of Asemanabad.

A source close to Naseri’s family, who is familiar with the matter, confirmed the news to HRANA and said: “On Sunday, August 23, 2026, a number of IRGC Intelligence agents entered Asemanabad, located in Ilam Province, to arrest Amin Naseri. During the arrest, an altercation occurred, and Mr. Naseri was shot and wounded. He was subsequently arrested and transferred to an undisclosed location.”

As of the time of this report, no information has been obtained regarding Naseri’s whereabouts or current condition.

Amin Naseri is a resident of Asemanabad, a city in Chardavol County, Ilam Province.
snippet: According to HRANA, Amin Naseri was arrested in the city of Asemanabad.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: Five Baha’i Citizens Arrested in Sari
content:
According to HRANA, on Saturday, August 22, 2026, four additional Baha’i citizens were arrested in Sari.

HRANA has verified the identities of these citizens as Maral Roshani, Negar Badiei, Shima Sanaei, and Fakhereh Zahedi. According to information received by HRANA, Maral Roshani and Negar Badiei were arrested by Security Police officers and, after several hours of interrogation, were released at approximately 7:00 p.m. the same day. The two women were instructed to report to the relevant authorities next Saturday for further questioning.

Shima Sanaei and Fakhereh Zahedi were also arrested by Ministry of Intelligence agents. In a phone call with their families, they stated that they are being held at the Ministry of Intelligence’s detention facility in Sari, known as the “Keshouei” detention facility.

Yesterday, HRANA reported the arrest of Soraya Manouchehrzadeh, a Baha’i citizen residing in Sari. Ms. Manouchehrzadeh was also arrested by Ministry of Intelligence agents and transferred to the Sari detention facility.
snippet: According to HRANA, on Saturday, August 22, 2026, four additional Baha’i citizens were arrested in Sari.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: Baha’i Citizen Soraya Manouchehrzadeh Arrested
content:
According to HRANA, Soraya Manouchehrzadeh, a Baha’i citizen residing in Sari, was arrested.

According to information received by HRANA, Ministry of Intelligence agents climbed over the wall of Ms. Manouchehrzadeh’s family home and entered the property without presenting a judicial warrant before arresting her.

During the operation, the agents also searched the home and confiscated a number of books and electronic devices belonging to Ms. Manouchehrzadeh and members of her family.

As of the time of this report, no information has been obtained regarding her place of detention, the charges against her, or her current condition.

In 2022, the home of this Baha’i citizen was also searched by security forces.

Over the past decade, Iran’s Baha’i community has been subjected to security and judicial actions more frequently than any other religious minority in the country. A review of HRA’s annual report reveals that over the past year an average of 62.41% of reports concerning religious minorities involved violations of the civil rights of Baha’is.
snippet: According to HRANA, Soraya Manouchehrzadeh, a Baha’i citizen residing in Sari, was arrested.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: New Case Filed in Prison: Hossein Shanbehzadeh Sentenced to One Year in Prison
content:
According to HRANA, Hossein Shanbehzadeh has been sentenced to prison.

According to the court ruling, the political prisoner was sentenced to one year of discretionary imprisonment on the charge of “disturbing public opinion through the dissemination of false information.” Amir Raisian, Shanbehzadeh’s defense attorney, announced the news and stated that the case was brought against his client over the release of an audio recording by Mr. Shanbehzadeh from inside prison.

Hossein Shanbehzadeh was arrested by security forces on June 4, 2024. He is currently serving his prison sentence in Evin Prison.

In September 2024, Branch 26 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court, presided over by Judge Iman Afshari, sentenced this political prisoner to five years in prison for “propaganda in favor of Israel,” four years for “insulting religious sanctities,” one year for “propaganda against the regime,” and two years in prison and a fine of 50 million tomans for “disseminating false information.”

Pursuant to Article 134 of the Islamic Penal Code, of the total 12-year prison sentence, the most severe punishment, five years’ imprisonment, is enforceable.
snippet: According to HRANA, Hossein Shanbehzadeh has been sentenced to prison.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: January 2026 Protests: Majid Adineh Executed
content:
According to HRANA, citing Mizan, Majid Adineh, one of those arrested during the nationwide protests of January 2026, was executed.

According to a report by the Judiciary’s Media Center, Mr. Adineh was arrested on the evening of January 9, 2026, in the Mohammadshahr area of Karaj by agents of the IRGC Intelligence Organization in Alborz Province. The outlet claimed that a firearm and several other pieces of equipment were discovered and seized from him at the time of his arrest.

According to the report, during the judicial proceedings, Majid Adineh faced charges including “taking operational action on behalf of hostile countries against national security and interests,” “moharebeh (enmity against God) through deliberate arson,” “assembly and collusion with the intent to commit a crime against national security,” “propaganda against the regime,” and unauthorized possession of a firearm, a stun gun, and tear-gas spray.
snippet: According to HRANA, citing Mizan, Majid Adineh, one of those arrested during the nationwide protests of January 2026, was executed.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: Supreme Court Upholds Death Sentence Against Arghavan Fallahi
content:
According to HRANA, the Supreme Court has upheld the death sentence issued against Arghavan Fallahi.

According to information received by HRANA, Fallahi was sentenced to death in July of this year on the charge of baghi (armed rebellion) by Judge Abolghasem Salavati, head of Branch 15 of the Tehran Revolutionary Court.

Following Israel’s attack on Evin Prison in June 2025, Fallahi was initially transferred to the Greater Tehran Prison and subsequently to Qarchak Prison in Varamin. She was later transferred back to Evin Prison.

Previously, an informed source told HRANA regarding the political prisoner’s situation: “Following her arrest, Ms. Fallahi spent some time in Wards 209 and 241 of Evin Prison, under the supervision of the Judiciary’s Intelligence Protection Organization. During this period, she was subjected to severe psychological torture, and attempts were made to extract forced confessions from her in connection with the assassinations of two judges, Mohammad Moghiseh and Ali Razini.”

Arghavan Fallahi was arrested by security forces in late January 2025 and transferred to the Ministry of Intelligence’s detention facility, known as Ward 209 of Evin Prison.
snippet: According to HRANA, the Supreme Court has upheld the death sentence issued against Arghavan Fallahi.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: Political Prisoner Masoumeh Sarban-Zadeh Held Without Furlough for Over a Year
content:
According to HRANA, Masoumeh Sarban-Zadeh is currently serving her sentence in Dowlatabad Prison in Isfahan.

According to information received by HRANA, Ms. Sarban-Zadeh was arrested by security forces in Najafabad, Isfahan Province, in June-July 2025. She was subsequently sentenced by a judicial authority to five years in prison on charges including “forming a group with the aim of disrupting national security.”

An informed source close to the political prisoner’s family confirmed the report and told HRANA: “Ms. Sarban-Zadeh, who is the mother of two children, has not been granted furlough despite more than a year having passed since her arrest and imprisonment.”

Sarban-Zadeh was arrested along with one of her daughters in June-July 2025 by security forces in connection with the 12-day war. During the judicial proceedings, her daughter was cleared of the allegation against her, acquitted, and released.

HRANA’s investigation into details of the current case, including the court or judicial authority that issued the sentence, remains ongoing.

Masoumeh Sarban-Zadeh, approximately 50 years old and a resident of Najafabad, is the mother of two daughters, approximately 14 and 18 years old.
snippet: According to HRANA, Masoumeh Sarban-Zadeh is currently serving her sentence in Dowlatabad Prison in Isfahan.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: Execution of Three Prisoners in Isfahan and Two in Ilam
content:
According to HRANA, citing Iran Human Rights Organization, on Wednesday, August 19, 2026, three prisoners were executed in Dastgerd Prison in Isfahan.

According to the report, the three prisoners were identified as Abdolbaset Barahouei, 30, from Zahedan; Omidreza Ghanbarian, 40, from Tabriz and the father of one child; and Amir Farhadi, from Isfahan.

Abdolbaset Barahouei was arrested in Isfahan in 2018 on charges related to drug offenses and was subsequently sentenced to death by a Revolutionary Court.

Mr. Ghanbarian was arrested five years ago, while Mr. Farhadi was arrested three years ago, both on charges related to drug offenses. They were subsequently sentenced to death by Revolutionary Courts.

Execution of Two Prisoners in Ilam Prison

According to Kurdpa, on the same day, two prisoners, including a woman, were executed in Ilam Prison.

The two prisoners were identified as Donya Mohammadi (female) and Khodadad Mohammadi, residents of Eyvan-e Gharb County.

According to the report, the two prisoners were arrested approximately two years ago in separate cases on murder charges and were subsequently sentenced to death by criminal courts.
snippet: According to HRANA, citing Iran Human Rights Organization, on Wednesday, August 19, 2026, three prisoners were executed in Dastgerd Prison in Isfahan.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: Letter from Prison: Ghazal Marzban Recounts Rape at a Ministry of Intelligence Detention Facility
content:
According to HRANA, Ghazal Marzban wrote in a letter, a copy of which was obtained by HRANA, that on May 17, 2023, while walking in a park, she was detained by several individuals and taken blindfolded to a location that she later learned was one of the Ministry of Intelligence’s operational detention facilities.

In describing what happened to her at the detention facility, she wrote that after being searched and forced to remove her clothes, she was left in a cell in the basement. According to Ms. Marzban, minutes later, a masked man entered the cell and raped her, an incident that, according to her account, resulted in bleeding as well as physical and psychological injuries. She further wrote that afterward, several officials at the detention facility promised to release her in exchange for her silence and, when releasing her, again threatened her against speaking about the incident.

title: January 2026 Protests: Ehsan Shams-Beigi Remains Detained in Legal Limbo for Over Seven Months
content:
According to HRANA, Ehsan Shams Beigi remains in detention without resolution of his legal status.

According to information received by HRANA, Mr. Shams Beigi has been held in legal limbo at Adelabad Prison in Shiraz for more than seven months. An indictment in his case on charges including “moharebeh (enmity against God),” “propaganda against the regime,” and “assembly and collusion against national security” had previously been referred to Branch 1 of the Shiraz Revolutionary Court, presided over by Judge Sadati. However, after reviewing the case, the court rejected the aforementioned charges and returned his case to Branch 8 of the Shiraz Public and Revolutionary Prosecutor’s Office for further investigation, under the supervision of investigator Mehrdad Molaei.

A source familiar with his situation, whose identity has been withheld by HRANA, said: “During his detention, Ehsan has been subjected to pressure and threats by Ministry of Intelligence agents on several occasions in an effort to extract forced confessions.”
snippet: According to HRANA, Ehsan Shams Beigi remains in detention without resolution of his legal status.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: Jamshid Molaei Arrested in Izeh County
content:
According to HRANA, Jamshid Molaei was arrested in Izeh.

Meisam Pirfalak, Kian Pirfalak’s father, announced the arrest of his relative Jamshid Molaei, known as Rayka, in a post.

According to him, the arrest took place one week after Kian’s gravesite was renovated, and no specific reason for the arrest has been announced so far. He also stated that Mr. Molaei has diabetes.

As of the time of this report, no precise information has been obtained regarding the agency responsible for his arrest, his place of detention, or the reasons for his arrest.

It should be noted that Kian Pirfalak, a 10-year-old child from Izeh, was killed by gunfire on November 16, 2022, during the nationwide protests in the city.
snippet:
According to HRANA, Jamshid Molaei was arrested in Izeh.

Meisam Pirfalak, Kian Pirfalak’s father, announced the arrest of his relative Jamshid Molaei, known as Rayka, in a post.

title: Zahra Rabbani Sentenced to Prison and Fines
content:
According to HRANA, citing Kolbar News, Zahra Rabbani has been sentenced to imprisonment and fines.

According to the report, Branch 107 of the Bojnurd Criminal Court II sentenced Rabbani to seven months and 16 days in prison on the charge of “assembly and collusion to commit a crime against the national security.” She was also sentenced to seven months and 16 days of imprisonment and a fine of one million tomans on the charge of “manufacturing explosive materials.” Additionally, on the charge of “carrying and distributing explosive materials,” she was fined four million tomans, along with an additional fine of one million tomans, equivalent to one to two times the value of the explosive materials.

Pursuant to Article 134 of the Islamic Penal Code, seven months and 16 days of her total prison sentence will be enforceable.

Zahra Rabbani was arrested by security forces on January 5, 2026. She was ultimately released in late February of that year after posting bail.
snippet: According to HRANA, citing Kolbar News, Zahra Rabbani has been sentenced to imprisonment and fines.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: January 2026 Protests: Pouria Hosseini-Mofard Sentenced to Death
content:
According to HRANA, Pouria Hosseini-Mofard, one of those arrested during the January 2026 protests, has been sentenced to death.

According to information received by HRANA, Mr. Hosseini-Mofard was sentenced to death by Branch 5 of the Mashhad Revolutionary Court, presided over by Judge Hossein Yazdankhah, with Seyed Reza Javad Mousavi serving as an advisory judge. The sentence was issued approximately one month ago.

The charges brought against Hosseini-Mofard include “acting against national security,” “assembly and collusion against national security,” and “operational acts disrupting the security of the country.” His case also alleges that the actions attributed to him were carried out in support of an opposition group.

An informed source told HRANA: “The alleged acts cited as the basis for the charges against this 23-year-old include breaking the glass of a bus stop and setting boxwood shrubs on fire after taking part in a protest organized in response to a public call.”

Pouria Hosseini-Mofard was arrested in Mashhad on January 14, 2026. After undergoing interrogation and judicial proceedings, he was transferred to Vakilabad Prison in Mashhad, where he remains detained.
snippet: According to HRANA, Pouria Hosseini-Mofard, one of those arrested during the January 2026 protests, has been sentenced to death.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency

title: January 2026 Protests: Ghaem Hosseini Executed
content:
According to HRANA, citing Mizan, the death sentence of Ghaem Hosseini, a foreign national and one of those arrested during the January 2026 protests in Isfahan, was carried out.

The Judiciary’s Media Center has claimed that four law enforcement officers were killed during the January 8, 2026 protests in Isfahan’s Alikhani Square. The institution further alleges that a number of protesters attacked law enforcement officers and damaged public property and facilities. The Judiciary has also alleged that, after attacking law enforcement personnel, the defendants in the case committed acts of violence, including setting fire to the bodies of those killed.
snippet: According to HRANA, citing Mizan, the death sentence of Ghaem Hosseini, a foreign national and one of those arrested during the January 2026 protests in Isfahan, was carried out.
sourceDescription: Human Rights Activists News Agency Hrana – News Agency | Human Rights Activists News Agency
